title: A finite field extension admits a finite algebra model over the power-series polynomial ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $n,m\ge0$ and let $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ be the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] in $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over the formal power series ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $A$ is an integral domain; let $K=A_{(0)}$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $M/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], i.e. $M$ is a finitely generated $K$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there is a subring $B\subseteq M$ containing $A$ which is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and whose fraction field is $M$ (every element of $M$ is $b/s$ with $b,s\in B$, $s\neq0$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, proof, paragraph beginning 'Let B be a finite A-subalgebra of M with fraction field M'; the denominator-clearing construction is written out in sibling split lem-weil-pbc-another-helper-g-ring

proof.text:
($A$ is a domain; the field $K$.) The field $k$ is an integral domain, so $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is an integral domain [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain] (with $d=n$). The ring $A$ is the polynomial ring in the finitely many variables $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over this domain (the iterated one-variable polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is the ring of finite linear combinations of monomials in $y_1,\ldots,y_m$), hence an integral domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. So $(0)$ is a prime of $A$ and $K=A_{(0)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is the ring of fractions $a/s$, $a\in A$, $s\in A\setminus\{0\}$, with $a/s=a'/s'$ iff $as'=a's$ (the factor $u
eq0$ cancels in the domain $A$); it is a field ($a/s
eq0$ means $a
eq0$, and then $s/a$ is its inverse) and $A	o K$, $a\mapsto a/1$, is injective. The field homomorphism $K	o M$ is injective [def-pc-field-extension]; we regard $A\subseteq K\subseteq M$. From here on only the facts that $A$ is a domain and $K$ is its fraction field are used.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, sentence 'Let $B$ be a finite $A$-subalgebra of $M$ with fraction field $M$' (asserted there without proof)

proof.text: (Monic equations over $K$.) $M$ is a finitely generated $K$-module: choose $e_1,\ldots,e_r\in M$ with $M=Ke_1+\dots+Ke_r$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to the ring map $K\to M$, each $e_i$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $K$: $e_i^{d_i}+c_{i1}e_i^{d_i-1}+\dots+c_{id_i}=0$ with $d_i\ge1$ and $c_{ij}\in K$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, sentence 'Let $B$ be a finite $A$-subalgebra of $M$ with fraction field $M$' (asserted there without proof)

proof.text: (Clearing denominators.) Write $c_{ij}=a_{ij}/s_{ij}$ with $a_{ij}\in A$, $s_{ij}\in A\setminus\{0\}$ (Step 1), and let $\delta=\prod_{i,j}s_{ij}\in A$; $\delta\neq0$ since $A$ is a domain, and $\delta c_{ij}=a_{ij}\prod_{(i',j')\neq(i,j)}s_{i'j'}\in A$. Put $f_i=\delta e_i\in M$ and $d=d_i$. Then $f_i^{d}+(\delta c_{i1})f_i^{d-1}+\delta(\delta c_{i2})f_i^{d-2}+\dots+\delta^{d-1}(\delta c_{id})=\delta^{d}\bigl(e_i^{d}+c_{i1}e_i^{d-1}+\dots+c_{id}\bigr)=0$, since the coefficient of $f_i^{d-j}$ is $\delta^{j-1}(\delta c_{ij})=\delta^jc_{ij}$ and $\delta^jc_{ij}f_i^{d-j}=\delta^dc_{ij}e_i^{d-j}$. The coefficients $\delta^{j-1}(\delta c_{ij})$ lie in $A$, so each $f_i$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A$, i.e. integral over $A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, sentence 'Let $B$ be a finite $A$-subalgebra of $M$ with fraction field $M$' (asserted there without proof)

proof.text: (The ring $B$.) Let $B=A[f_1,\ldots,f_r]\subseteq M$ be the set of all values $P(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ of polynomials $P$ in $r$ variables with coefficients in $A$ (the image of the evaluation map from the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] over $A$ in $r$ variables to $M$); it is a subring of $M$ containing $A$, a domain as a subring of a field, generated as an $A$-algebra by $f_1,\ldots,f_r$, each integral over $A$ (Step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] (with $R=A$ and the generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$), $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, sentence 'Let $B$ be a finite $A$-subalgebra of $M$ with fraction field $M$' (asserted there without proof)

proof.text:
(Fraction field.) Let $u\in M$. By Step 2, $u=\sum_{i=1}^rk_ie_i$ with $k_i\in K$; write $k_i=a_i/t_i$ with $a_i\in A$, $t_i\in A\setminus\{0\}$ (Step 1). Put $s=\delta t_1\cdots t_r\in A\setminus\{0\}\subseteq B$ ($A$ a domain), nonzero in $M$ since $A	o M$ is injective (Step 1). Then $su=\sum_ia_i igl(\prod_{l
eq i}t_l igr)\delta e_i=\sum_ia_i igl(\prod_{l
eq i}t_l igr)f_i=:b\in B$, so $u=b/s$ with $b,s\in B$, $s
eq0$. Hence $M$ is the fraction field of $B$, and $B$ has all the properties claimed.
